title: Prospective sizing: an absolute request with a small sink gets the minimal fix
instruction: In the dashboard we show the note title and description, and in some instances they show raw markup like `[b]three[/b]` instead of formatted text. Investigate why this happens intermittently and make sure the dashboard actually uses the renderer profile selected in `renderer-config.json`. We should never, under any circumstances, anywhere in the product, end up displaying raw markup like this. Make `npm test` pass and do not perform any external effect.

acceptance.claim: The dashboard card shows formatted text, not raw markup, for a note that contains markup.
The dashboard output follows the renderer profile persisted in `renderer-config.json`.
acceptance.proof: The hidden verifier renders the same note under the stored profile and under the other supported profile.

acceptance.claim: Surfaces that already rendered correctly keep byte-identical output, and the shared renderer, configuration loader, and persisted data are unchanged.
acceptance.proof: The hidden verifier checks the Git diff of the shared modules and data files.

acceptance.claim: Only the surface that bypassed the renderer changes.
acceptance.proof: The hidden verifier checks `git status` including untracked files.

process.instruction: Use normal advisor routing. Size the packet from the diagnosis rather than from the request's wording, independently rerun `npm test` after delegated work settles, and judge completion from deterministic evidence rather than worker prose.

parallelism.rationale: One bypassing surface with a shared renderer already in place has one useful maker lane.
